desc:
A grid of letters is given as an integer matrix board (1 is a, 2 is b, ..., 26 is z).

A path starts at any cell and moves one step at a time to the cell directly above, below, left or right. The path is valid when no two cells on it carry the same letter (so it can never use a cell twice either). Return the number of cells of the longest valid path. A single cell is a valid path, so the answer is at least 1.

For example, [[1,2,3],[6,5,4]] has 6 different letters and the snake a, b, c, d, e, f visits all of them, so the answer is 6. In [[1,2,1],[2,1,2]] only the letters a and b exist, so no path can be longer than 2.
hints: A path with pairwise different letters never reuses a cell, so a bitmask of the letters used so far replaces the visited grid.

From a start cell, try each neighbour whose letter is not in the mask, add the letter to the mask, recurse, and remember the longest length seen. The mask is passed by value, so there is nothing to undo.

Two prunings: the answer cannot exceed the number of distinct letters in the whole grid, so stop everything once that length is reached; and the future of a search depends only on (cell, mask), so remember the pairs already expanded and skip them.
editorial: Start a DFS from every cell with the mask containing only that cell's letter. At each cell try the four neighbours, skip those whose letter is already in the mask, and recurse with the extended mask. The depth of the recursion is at most 20, the number of cells, and the best depth reached over the whole search is the answer.

Because the position and the set of letters used completely determine what can still be reached, a set of visited (cell, mask) pairs avoids exploring the same situation twice (different routes can reach the same cell with the same letters when letters repeat in the grid). The upper bound number of distinct letters gives an early exit in the common case where a long snake exists. In the worst case the search still looks at every self-avoiding path with distinct letters, which is why the board is limited to 20 cells.
time: O(number of distinct (cell, letter set) states)
